fields.headline: STATE TO SPEND UP TO $6.5M ON IDENTITY CHECKS
fields.deck: The award to Paravision runs through September 2031.

frames.mediaQuery: Paravision facial recognition liveness detection identity verification

stories.caption:
The U.S. State Department has awarded facial recognition developer Paravision a firm-fixed-price contract worth up to $6.5 million. The department awarded it September 23 and initially obligated $1.3 million. The contract can run through September 22, 2031.

The State Department competed the work under simplified acquisition procedures as a total small-business set-aside, and it received a single offer. The contract is described in procurement records as "digital detection/identity assurance."

Public award records do not identify which Paravision products were bought. The description overlaps with the company's deepfake detection, passive liveness detection and facial recognition offerings, but the record does not confirm which, if any, were included. Separately, the department made a $24,717 purchase on April 30 for a "purchase card for software license," and records do not show whether that purchase was related to the September award.

Source: Biometric Update, October 17, 2026

fields.headline: XTEND SECURES 6,000 STRIKER SYSTEMS ORDER
fields.deck: The $40.5 million award follows a Gauntlet II result in the Close Quarters Battle segment.

frames.mediaQuery: XTEND STRIKER drone close quarters battle

stories.caption:
XTEND AI Robotics has received a $40.5 million order for 6,000 STRIKER systems, according to a company press release dated October 13, 2026. The award comes after XTEND was named a top performer in the Close Quarters Battle segment of Gauntlet II, part of the Department of War's Drone Dominance Program, which the company describes as an iterative $1 billion effort. The company also said it expects to deliver the systems under the order.

STRIKER runs on XTEND's proprietary XOS operating system and is built for tactical work in confined, complex and GNSS-denied spaces. In the same release, XTEND gave preliminary third quarter 2026 revenue and an update on its backlog. CEO Aviv Shapira said the company "competed, proved our capabilities, and now we are ready to build."

XTEND moves directly into Gauntlet III in the Close Quarters Battle segment of Phase 3, which the Department of War opened on September 28, 2026. Gauntlet II awardees skip the open solicitation and Pitch & Fly stages, but they must first fulfill a 400-system production order. Gauntlet III performance will decide whether any Phase 3 orders are placed, and taking part does not guarantee an award.

Source: XTEND, 13 October 2026

stories.caption:
MISSION BRIEF // COYOTE / RAYTHEON

//Raytheon

📍Tucson, AZ

Tech: Counter-drone interceptor

Platform: Interceptor missile

Goal: Defeat current and emerging drone threats with a Coyote upgrade.

Why: A rocket motor aims to speed launch, flight and successive shots.

Traction: Coyote Block 2C+RM completed three Raytheon-funded developmental tests, with the first launches of a Coyote fitted with a tactical rocket motor, per Raytheon.

Raytheon, an RTX business, said the Block 2C+RM upgrade is advancing from concept to testing in 15 months. The effort builds on current Coyote variants, which the company says have intercepted hundreds of drones in combat. The upgrade integrates a rocket motor, a new seeker and a new warhead.

The initial test series confirmed initial integration with the current counter-drone architecture. Raytheon says the program is part of an urgent joint U.S. military mission against evolving drone threats.

Source: RTX, 12OCT26

Image: U.S. Army photo by Staff Sgt. Fred Brown

fields.headline: ARMY TO TEST COUNTER-DRONE TECH IN AFRICA
fields.deck: The partnership aims to deliver tested systems to Soldiers within 180 days.

stories.caption:
The U.S. Army's Southern European Task Force, Africa is working with the Global Tactical Edge Acquisition Directorate, or G-TEAD, to put new systems through trials on the continent and get them into Soldiers' hands within six months.

The first accelerated capability event, or ACE, is set for spring 2027 in Tan-Tan, Morocco. It targets counter-unmanned aircraft systems and force protection, with a focus on shielding early-entry command posts and operating locations from Group 1–3 small UAS. The Army says Africa's open spectrum and uncongested airspace give Soldiers room to validate solutions that ranges in the United States and Europe cannot easily replicate.

G-TEAD assigned a team to the task force this summer to link urgent operational needs with rapid acquisition money. A three-phase ACE model moves from submission and preparation to Soldier-led demonstrations and then operational evaluation. Demonstrations are planned for early 2027 in Morocco, with an assessment in the spring during the next African Lion exercise. G-TEAD will validate up to 15 solutions, with PAE Fires serving as the transition partner.

Source: U.S. Army, October 16, 2026

Image: U.S. Army photo by Sgt. 1st Class Rodney Roldan

fields.headline: OSC OFFERS ANTHEIA UP TO $80M LOAN
fields.deck: The conditional loan would support Antheia's U.S. plan to onshore critical drug ingredients.

stories.caption:
The Department of War's Office of Strategic Capital has issued a conditional commitment for a direct, long-term loan of up to $80 million to Antheia, a Menlo Park, Calif., advanced biosynthesis company. The financing, alongside additional private capital, would support Antheia's U.S. manufacturing strategy to onshore production of critical pharmaceutical ingredients.

The U.S. relies on foreign countries for about 90 percent of its supply of key starting materials and active pharmaceutical ingredients, according to the Department of War's announcement. The company says that dependence leaves Americans highly vulnerable to drug shortages.

This is a conditional commitment, not final financing. Antheia must complete additional steps before financial close, including financial, legal, technical, investment and due diligence requirements. To date, the company has also received $32 million in non-dilutive federal financing and equity from strategic government-affiliated investors.

Source: PR Newswire (company release) and U.S. Department of War, Oct. 18, 2026
